title: Rebuild sutra_orient conventions section on the deviation engine
description:
Per the sutra/176 decision (arc sutra/~12): rebuild `sutra_orient`'s convention section as a descriptive "what's normal here" summary computed from the same group-by/pattern engine as the review deviation report — no persisted lifecycle, no preferred/proposal/waiver/template surfacing (those subsystems are gone after demolition).

Content per scope/component: the strongest identity→obligation patterns with counts ("15/15 Db methods take &self and return Result") plus 1-2 exemplar symbol pointers each. Cap for context economy — orient is core tier and gets read at session start.

Perf note: orient is core tier (no analysis pass required). If on-the-fly attribute extraction per call is too slow for large components, use the ephemeral conventions cache decided in the review-deviation task; do not reintroduce durable persistence.

This section's continued existence is provisional — the validation phase (HITL task on this arc) decides whether agents actually use it. Build it thin.

Acceptance: orient output for a component shows top patterns with counts + exemplars and nothing from the deleted subsystems; orient latency unchanged in order of magnitude; conventions-map.md orient section updated.

messages.author: codex
messages.text: Codex review: approve with notes. Two findings addressed in 9309a31:\n- (medium) `db.all_files()` was called inside the per-component loop — hoisted to reuse the existing `all_files` from handle scope.\n- (low) conventions table purpose in conventions-map.md still said \"persisted for orient\" — corrected to \"persisted for sutra_conventions list\".
